question: According to the WHO classification, diarrhoea lasting between 14 and 28 days is termed:

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Acute diarrhoea is defined as lasting fewer than 14 days.
Correct. Persistent diarrhoea spans 14–28 days; it is an important category in Indian public health as it is associated with malnutrition in children.
Chronic diarrhoea is defined as lasting more than 4 weeks (>28 days).
Dysentery refers to diarrhoea with blood and/or mucus — it is a qualitative, not a duration-based, classification.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the WHO duration-based classification: acute <14 days, persistent 14–28 days, chronic >4 weeks.
Well done. The three duration categories — acute (<14 days), persistent (14–28 days), and chronic (>4 weeks) — are fundamental to diarrhoeal disease classification.
